title: Density of sparse de Bruijn characteristic functions
summary: Determine the density of de Bruijn generators among characteristic functions having a uniform per-degree cap on their algebraic-normal-form terms.

formal_statement.body: For admissible $n$ and $k$, let $\mathcal S_{n,k}$ contain the Boolean functions $$f(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=x_0+g(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1})+x_n$$ for which the algebraic normal form of $g$ has at most $k$ monomials of each degree. Determine, exactly or with a complete asymptotic characterization, the density $$\frac{|\{f\in\mathcal S_{n,k}:f\text{ generates a de Bruijn sequence}\}|}{|\mathcal S_{n,k}|}.$$

scope.domain: Sparse Boolean characteristic functions of binary de Bruijn sequences
assumptions: For every degree, $g$ contains at most $k$ algebraic-normal-form monomials
The numerator counts functions that generate de Bruijn sequences
scope.unresolved_remainder: For general admissible $(n,k)$, neither the exact density nor a complete asymptotic law is known. Later work on linear parts, second-highest degree, or total term count does not determine any instance of the simultaneous per-degree-cap density.
